front: Why do $f$ and $f+m f_s$ give the same samples?
back: $e^{i2\pi m n}=1$: the extra $m f_s$ adds whole turns between consecutive samples.

front: SNR of a $b$-bit quantised sine of amplitude $A$
back: $6.02\,b+1.76+20\log_{10}A$ dB; about 6 dB per bit, 96 dB at 16 bits.

$X[k]=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}x[n]e^{-i2\pi kn/N}$: correlation with a sinusoid that makes $k$ turns over the frame.

front: Frequency of DFT bin $k$ and resolution
Why only $N/2+1$ bins for real signals?
back: Conjugate symmetry $X[N-k]=\overline{X[k]}$ makes the upper half redundant (`np.fft.rfft`).
$T=1+\lfloor(L-N)/H\rfloor$ for signal length $L$, frame $N$, hop $H$; e.g. 10 s, 400/160 at 16 kHz gives 998.
Energy of a tone spreading to far-away bins because a frame has abrupt edges; tapering with a window reduces it.
$X[t,k]=\sum_n w[n]x[tH+n]e^{-i2\pi kn/N}$; complex matrix of shape $(T, N/2+1)$.
Window of $N/f_s$ seconds resolves $f_s/N$ Hz: long windows give fine pitch but blurry timing, short windows the reverse.
